walkthroughs.body_html:
In November 1918 Germany lost the war and Kaiser Wilhelm II abdicated.

Ebert's new Weimar Republic signed the armistice on 11 November. Many Germans called the leaders November Criminals for the 'stab in the back' myth.

The Treaty of Versailles forced Germany to: lose 13% of land, pay £6.6 billion in reparations, cap its army at 100,000, and accept war guilt under Article 231.

Most Germans called it a Diktat — a dictated peace.

Germany missed a reparations payment. France occupied the Ruhr in January 1923.

The government printed money to pay strikers — triggering hyperinflation. In November Hitler tried his Beer Hall Putsch in Munich. It failed and he was jailed, writing Mein Kampf.

options: Article 48
Article 231
Article 14
Article 25

options: Berlin
Munich
Weimar
Hamburg

mcqs.q: What caused the German hyperinflation of 1923?
options: The government printing money to pay striking workers during the French occupation of the Ruhr, on top of existing reparations and war debts.
Hitler won an outright majority in the 1932 presidential election.
Reparations alone caused the hyperinflation.
The hyperinflation was caused by the Wall Street Crash.

mcqs.q: Why did the Treaty of Versailles cause resentment in Germany?
options: The hyperinflation was caused by the Wall Street Crash.
Because Germany was not invited to sign it.
Because Germany lost more soldiers than any other country in the war.
It assigned sole war guilt to Germany (Article 231) and imposed harsh reparations, territorial losses and military restrictions.

mcqs.q: How did Hitler come to power in 1933?
options: Hitler won an outright majority in the 1932 presidential election.
Hitler seized power through a violent coup or revolution.
He was legally appointed Chancellor by President Hindenburg as part of a conservative political deal, after the Nazis became the largest party in the Reichstag.
The hyperinflation was caused by the Wall Street Crash.
